newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mostly down, market seen dull.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mostly down, market seen dull.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly lower on Friday on halved volume and turnover but traders did not expect stronger movements on the market.
"There won't be any big boom on the market in the nearer future. The prices might go down just a bit more, but then trading will pick up," said a trader with a large market share.
Things were not likely to improve due to a seasonal lull, he said adding that Friday's trade was diminished partly because foreign investors held back after the latest political stirrings.
Croatian customs confiscated $65,000 in cash coming into the country for the local branch of the Soros foundation and briefly detained two of its officials for questioning on Friday morning.
Four of eight active issues fell, two were up and two flat.
Volume was halved to 3,432 shares and turnover shrank to 2.9 million kuna from 7.9 million. The week's turnover of 22.3 million was down from 29 million last week.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, down 10 kuna to 980, was the most actively traded issue with 1,430 units sold.
Its E-series was the biggest gainer, rising 10 kuna to 430 on volume of 158 shares.
Hotelier Laguna led decliners, which also included Kras chocolate maker and food processor Podravka. Laguna lost 50 kuna down to 1,050 on volume of 70 shares.
Second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded at 7.15 percent above par, compared to 5.0 percent last week on total turnover of 3.8 million kuna.
